content:
If you're like me, you've probably spent way too much time on Wikipedia, clicking from one article to another and falling down rabbit holes. Now, finally, there's an official app—err, widget—for that.

There's finally a button that takes you to a random Wikipedia article with a single tap.

Today, Wikipedia updated its iOS app to include a pretty fun and useful new thing: a "Random Article" widget you can place on your iPhone and iPad home screen.

The widget comes in two sizes (small and medium), and there's a cute mascot to keep you company.

Tap the widget, and you'll jump straight into a completely random Wikipedia article, automatically entering Random mode.

No need to leave the app and tap the widget again. Just hit the Random button and it'll roll the dice for you with a new article, letting you go even deeper down this "random rabbit hole."

Enjoy yourself, but try not to get too carried away! Earlier this summer, the Wikipedia app already added a historical trivia quiz game.

You can find this new widget in today's update of the Wikipedia iPhone and iPad app.
